title: SLO Rhythm and Dependency Deep Dive Brief
summary: This brief captures a pragmatic 90-day micro-iteration plan to align engineering, product, and platform teams around a repeatable SLO rhythm and to remove critical cross-team dependencies that block SLO adoption for model-serving endpoints.
objectives: 1) Establish a lightweight SLO cadence (define-measure-act) for 3 pilot services. 2) Remove top 5 observability and dependency blockers that cause signal gaps. 3) Create minimal runbooks and an onboarding template so feature teams can adopt SLOs without SRE hand-holding.
scope: Pilot limited to model-serving infra (hosted-api + dedicated pools) and two UX-facing product routes (chat-generation, embeddings). Non-goal: full org-wide SLO rollout and long-term capacity redesigns.
stakeholders: Product: Priya Rao (hosted-api PM), Eng: Elliot Chen (serving runtime lead), Platform: Diego Martinez, SRE: Aisha Patel (project lead), Observability: Marta Kovacs, Customer Success: Lina Goldberg (advisory)
approach_summary: Use small timeboxed experiments (2-week sprints) focused on signal completeness and dependency unwinding. Each sprint produces a tangible artifact: SLA->SLO translation for a route, one instrumentation PR, and a runbook. Emphasize measurable signals (p95 latency, error-rate by codepath, queueing depth) and automated gating for rollouts.
milestones: Week 0: Kickoff, finalize pilot services, map dependencies (datastores, feature flags, model variants)
Week 2: Signal inventory complete; missing metrics and gaps identified; ownership assigned
Week 4: Instrumentation PRs for host-level metrics and trace points merged for pilot services
Week 6: Define SLO targets and error budgets for pilots; create per-route dashboards and alert guards
Week 8: Runbook templates and onboarding checklist published; initial A/B canary guided by SLOs
Week 10: Dependency remediation sprint complete (3 critical deps resolved); automation for error-budget burn alerts wired
Week 12: Pilot retro, decision checkpoint: expand, iterate, or pause; rollout plan drafted for next 90 days
deliverables: 1) Signal inventory spreadsheet (linked), 2) Three per-route SLO definitions and dashboards, 3) Instrumentation PRs, 4) Runbook template and oncall playbook excerpt, 5) Decision log with next-step recommendation
metrics_and_success_criteria: Adoption: 3 feature teams able to declare SLOs and own dashboards within 12 weeks. Signal completeness: reduce "signal gaps" (missing span-level traces or missing error counters) by 80% for pilots. Operational: Mean time to detect (MTTD) for SLO breaches <= 3 minutes; Mean time to mitigate (MTTM) within 45 minutes on average during pilot incidents.
decision_points: - After week 6: decide whether SLO targets need to be relaxed for UX (latency) vs strict for correctness (error-rate). - After week 12: go/no-go to scale cadence to additional services and invest in observability platform quotas.
communication_plan: Weekly 30-minute sync (SRE + product + platform) with a public readout doc. Biweekly stakeholder digest emailed to exec sponsors and CS with highlights: burn-rate, recent incidents, dependency progress.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Observability budget/retention limits cause missing historical data. Mitigation: short-term reduce retention to critical metrics and stream aggregated summaries to cheaper buckets.
Risk: Feature teams deprioritize instrumentation. Mitigation: pair engineers from platform to land the first PRs and add instrumentation tasks to sprint commitments for product owners.
Risk: SLO churn leads to noisy alerts. Mitigation: introduce a stability window and auto-suppress newly created alerts for 24 hours; require a postmortem for repeated flapping.
Risk: Dependence on legacy job that cannot be modified quickly. Mitigation: isolate with a compatibility proxy and add safety timeouts while product remediates.
Risk: Customer-impact mapping ambiguous for ML outputs. Mitigation: define conservative user-impact heuristics (e.g., hallucination rate proxy via rerank failure signals) and iterate with CS.
runbook_snippet: If SLO breach (error budget burn > 5% in last 15m): 1) Pager SRE rotation and platform lead, 2) Abort canary traffic and route to fallback model variant, 3) Run quick automated diagnostic: tail error logs, check KV cache hit rate, check upstream model pool health, 4) If degradation tied to model variant, escalate to applied-ml for rollback.
dependency_unwinding_actions: 1) Inventory external deps and map owners, 2) For each dep classify as: controllable / partner / legacy, 3) Create a remediation lane: observability (add metrics), contract (SLAs), fallback (proxy or cache), 4) Triage top-5 by customer-impact and effort and schedule in sprint 3
experiments_and_sweeps: A) Auto-batching volume experiment: measure p95 change and cost per token across two batching configs. B) Cache warming sweep: instrument prefix-cache hit vs cold-start latency and tie to SLOs. C) Canary rollback threshold tuning: find the error-budget-based cutoff that minimizes user-visible failures while maximizing capacity use.
next_steps: 1) Share this brief with stakeholders and collect feedback by EOD Friday, 2) Confirm pilot service owners and add signal inventory tasks to sprint board, 3) Book two 1:1s between platform and product to unblock dep owners
notes: This doc intentionally prescribes minimal viable artifacts — the goal is to create a repeatable cadence where each cycle creates operational value and reduces SRE handoffs. Treat SLOs as a coordination mechanism, not a punitive metric.
